question.text: Chola Private Capital LVF (Large Value Fund for Accredited Investors) is a Category II AIF. Each investor has committed at least INR 25 crore. What is the single-investee company cap applicable to this LVF, and what is its minimum AI ticket?

answer.text: Single-investee cap 25%; minimum AI commitment INR 1 crore
Single-investee cap 100%; minimum AI commitment INR 10 crore
Single-investee cap 75%; minimum AI commitment INR 70 crore
Single-investee cap 50%; minimum AI commitment INR 25 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the LVF framework (SEBI (AIF) (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2021 and subsequent amendments), Large Value Funds for Accredited Investors enjoy relaxed concentration — up to 50% of investable funds may be deployed in a single investee company (vs 25% standard Cat I/II cap). Each AI in an LVF must commit no less than INR 25 crore (other than Manager/Sponsor/employees). The Trap: Option A applies the standard Cat I/II numbers, ignoring the LVF relaxation. Option B invents '100%' — nothing in regulation permits full single-investee concentration. Option C mixes up numbers with Special Situation Fund structures. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests LVF extensively (both Cat I/II and Cat III versions). XIX-A Distributors must understand LVF to sell to HNI/family offices. AI framework runs across exams — XXI-B portfolio managers have their own AI relaxations for minimum INR 50 lakh threshold waiver. Manager's Pro-Tip: LVF is the go-to vehicle for concentrated late-stage PE strategies and distressed-asset plays — the 50% cap allows club-deals and co-investment structures to hold meaningful stakes. In PPM, clearly disclose that consents for associate transactions still require 75% investor approval (Reg 15(2)).
